lines: I remember sinking far below myself. You hauled the line in.
The dark had me hooked. You cut the line clean.
I knew your voice before I could remember your name.
You stayed close when I was dangerous. I will not forget that.
The first clear thing I remember is your hand holding the cure.
My thoughts came back slowly, like shore through morning fog.
I owe you more than a basket of fish can cover.
I woke hungry, frightened, and myself again because of you.
The dock boards felt familiar before any faces did.
I can work, eat, and sleep normally again. That is your doing.
Some of that sickness is still missing from my memory. I am glad you are not.
You brought me home when I could not find the way myself.
I remember reaching for the boat rope and hearing you tell me to hold on.
Food tasted right the morning after you cured me. I nearly cried over soup.
My hands stopped shaking when I realized the village was safe around me.
You risked being bitten to give me another life.
I may never remember every moment, but I remember who saved me.
The river sounds peaceful again instead of distant and wrong.
I have slept better each night since you helped me.
Thank you. I mean it more deeply than I know how to say.
Your face breaks the surface of that memory, then slips under again.
I remember a taste like bad river water, then breathing like it was new.
You were there when I woke, were you not?
I know you helped me. The rest comes back in pieces.
Your voice is familiar, but I cannot place where I heard it.
Was I near the dock when you found me?
The cure worked. My memory is taking longer.
I remember cold hands and someone telling me to swallow.
Some days I know exactly what happened. Other days it feels like a story about someone else.
I recognized my nets before I recognized half the village.
You look important to that missing part of my memory.
Did you pull me away from the water, or am I mixing two nights together?
I keep seeing a bottle in your hand when I close my eyes.
The smell of the boat rope brought one small piece back this morning.
I am grateful. I only wish I understood what for.
People say you saved me, and I believe them.
My hands remember knots that my mind cannot name yet.
I woke with mud on my clothes and no idea how it got there.
Please be patient if I ask the same thing twice.
The fog is lifting, just not all at once.
I remember you through deep water and panic. Do not crowd the bank.
I know you helped me. I also remember why my hands still shake.
The cure left me frightened of anyone standing too close.
Stay there. I can thank you from here.
Part of me knows you are safe. The rest has not caught up.
I remember your face beside something terrible.
Give me room to breathe and I will try to talk.
I am grateful, but I am not ready to be touched.
Your voice brings back the cure and the fear around it.
I woke swinging at everyone near me. I do not want that to happen again.
Do not come behind me. I still startle too easily.
I remember biting down on glass and hearing you shout.
You saved me, but the memory does not feel gentle.
I need the open dock between us for now.
Some nights I wake certain the sickness has returned.
Let me see both your hands while we speak.
I am trying to separate what you did from what happened to me.
The smell of that potion still turns my stomach.
I will trust my own mind again eventually. Today is not that day.
Thank you for the cure. Now please step back.
